channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula deve receber Alcolumbre para conversa no Alvorada após dois meses e meio sem falar com ele
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has agreed to hold a private meeting with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre after two and a half months of strained relations, with the encounter expected to take place this week at the Palácio da Alvorada. The meeting aims to ease tensions between the Executive and Legislative branches, particularly over the PEC to end the 6x1 work schedule — a key re-election pledge of Lula that Alcolumbre has yet to bring to a vote in the Senate. Government leaders, including Camilo Santana and José Guimarães, are pushing for dialogue to avoid confrontation, despite some PT members labeling Alcolumbre an 'enemy of workers' if he continues to block the proposal.

item.title: Ao tratar de tarifaço dos EUA, Caiado critica Lula por 'provocar' Trump e 'ajoelhamento' de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized President Lula for provoking Donald Trump to gain electoral advantage and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for sending a document to the U.S. government requesting a delay in tariffs on Brazilian products until the October elections, which Caiado described as 'kneeling' to U.S. interests. He argued Brazil must adopt a sovereign and technically grounded stance in negotiations, advocating for the strengthening of the Itamaraty and rejecting both provocation and submission in foreign policy.

item.title: Procuradoria vê propaganda eleitoral antecipada em fala de Lula sobre pré-candidatas ao Senado
item.description: The Electoral Prosecutor's Office in São Paulo recommended the conviction of President Lula and former ministers Simone Tebet and Marina Silva for alleged premature electoral campaigning during a May government event, where he explicitly asked for votes for the two Senate pre-candidates.

item.title: O aceno de Camilo Santana a Alcolumbre após assumir a liderança do governo no Senado
item.description: Senator Camilo Santana (PT-CE) assumed the government leadership in the Senate and extended an overture to Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), calling for dialogue and humility to repair relations after the rejection of Jorge Messias to the STF. He emphasized the need to advance key agendas like ending the 6×1 work scale and the Security PEC, amid rising tensions, including threats from the PT leader in the Chamber to label Alcolumbre an 'enemy of workers'.

item.title: Campanha eleitoral caminha para bater o recorde de mediocridade política
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian electoral campaign is heading toward a record of political mediocrity, reflecting a broader institutional crisis that extends beyond the Executive and Legislative branches to include eroding trust in the Judiciary. Despite structural advantages such as natural resources, a large domestic market, and skilled human capital, public debate remains trapped in sterile polarization, ignoring structural challenges like demography, productivity, organized crime, and external vulnerability. The prevailing perception is that both the exhausted government and a familistic, morally questionable opposition lack ideas and integrity, making solutions to major problems increasingly elusive.

item.title: PDT espera Lula em convenção nacional do partido após atritos com PT
item.description: The PDT confirmed President Lula's (PT) attendance at its national convention on July 20 in Brasília, following recent tensions over state-level alliances. The party seeks to strengthen its position on Fernando Haddad's ticket for São Paulo governor, demanding the first Senate substitute slot. Despite strains — including Lupi's dismissal from the Ministry of Social Security over the INSS scandal — the PDT aims to maintain the progressive front, as seen in Rio Grande do Sul, where it stepped back to support Juliana Brizola's candidacy.

item.title: Senado aprova projeto que amplia crédito a exportadores
item.description: The Senate approved PLV 7/2026, expanding credit for Brazilian exporters through the Brazil Soberano program, offering up to R$15 billion in financing managed by BNDES with risk coverage from FGE. Derived from MP 1.345/2026, the measure was broadened to include agribusiness exporters and associative entities to strengthen resilience against trade shocks such as U.S. tariffs and the Iran war.

item.title: Procuradoria eleitoral vê propaganda antecipada em fala de Lula sobre Tebet e Marina
item.description: The São Paulo Electoral Prosecutor's Office determined that President Lula's statement on May 19, during the launch of the Move Aplicativos program, constituted illegal early electioneering by explicitly requesting votes for Simone Tebet and Marina Silva, who are Senate pre-candidates. Electoral law prohibits explicit vote requests before August 16 of the election year. The final decision rests with the TRE-SP plenary, pending the opinion of reporting judge Danyelle Galvão.

item.title: 'Não podemos sair brigando dentro de casa', diz presidente do PL sobre atritos entre Michelle e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The national president of the PL, Valdemar Costa Neto, stated that Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro are not speaking after social media accusations and stressed the need to resolve internal conflicts within 20 days to set a direction ahead of the party's national convention on July 25. He praised Michelle as a special leader and noted that the vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket remains undefined, emphasizing the need for someone with electoral support and rejecting Daniella Marques due to her lack of votes, despite calling her an excellent person.

item.title: Ibaneis Rocha desiste de concorrer ao Senado pelo Distrito Federal
item.description: Ibaneis Rocha withdrew from the Senate race in the Federal District following the Banco Master scandal, citing family and legal work as reasons. His decision comes amid investigations into the attempted purchase of Banco Master by BRB during his governorship, which caused billions in losses. The withdrawal weakens the right-wing bloc in the DF, especially as Michelle Bolsonaro may also drop out due to internal PL conflicts.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro propõe criação de zona de livre comércio com os EUA e critica relação de Lula com a China
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) proposed the creation of a free trade zone between Brazil and the United States, suggesting Brazil’s inclusion in an agreement similar to USMCA, which he referred to as 'Afta' (Free Trade Agreement of the Americas). During a live stream, he criticized the Lula government for 'licking China’s boots' and prioritizing ideology over national interests, claiming he went to the U.S. to protect Brazil from tariffs and from Lula himself. He also defended the Pix payment system as a Bolsonaro-era initiative and cited corruption scandals involving the current administration.

item.title: Flávio propõe acordo de livre-comércio entre Brasil e EUA
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro proposed Brazil's inclusion in a free-trade agreement modeled after NAFTA, suggesting the creation of an 'Americas Free Trade Agreement' (AFTA) with the U.S., Mexico, and Canada, citing the recent U.S.-Argentina deal as a reference. He criticized the Lula government for failing to send representatives to USTR hearings in Washington, arguing Brazil must be present to defend its interests and attract American investment.

item.title: STF confirma constitucionalidade de repasses mínimos de 30% para cotas raciais nas eleições
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) upheld the constitutionality of Constitutional Amendment No. 133/2024, which establishes a minimum 30% allocation of the Special Campaign Financing Fund (FEFC) and the Party Fund for Black and mixed-race candidates in elections. The ruling rejected petitions from entities arguing for a higher percentage, such as 55.5% proportional to the Afro-descendant population, stating that defining the index is a legislative prerogative, while the STF only assesses constitutionality. The 30% floor is mandatory, but parties may increase it voluntarily.

item.title: TSE devolve Alex Manente à presidência nacional do Cidadania até as eleições
item.description: TSE President Minister Nunes Marques ordered the return of Alex Manente to the national presidency of the Cidadania party until the 2026 elections, in a preliminary injunction. The measure aims to ensure party stability during the electoral process.

item.title: Motta indica Mendonça Filho como relator da PEC que reduz a maioridade penal
item.description: Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), president of the Chamber of Deputies, appointed Deputy Mendonça Filho (PL-PE) as rapporteur for the PEC reducing the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16. Deputy Aluisio Mendes (Republicanos-MA) will preside over the special committee tasked with debating the proposal, set to convene in the second week of August. The measure, already approved by the Constitution and Justice Committee, would allow 16-year-olds to be criminally liable and serve sentences in the regular prison system.

item.title: Como está a aprovação do governo Lula na nova pesquisa Meio/Ideia
item.description: The Meio/Ideia poll from July 2026 shows President Lula with 46.5% approval and 48.5% disapproval, a difference within the 2.5 pp margin of error. The government is rated as bad/terrible by 41%, good/excellent by 32.5%, and regular by 24.5%; 51% of voters say Lula does not deserve another term, compared to 45.7% who believe he does.

item.title: Congresso aprova MP que destina à PF parte da arrecadação com bets
item.description: Congress approved a provisional measure allocating 3% of federal revenue from fixed-odds sports betting (bets) to the Funapol fund of the Federal Police to cover health expenses for its agents. The allocation will be phased: 1% in 2026, 2% in 2027, and 3% from 2028 onward, with an additional authorization of up to R$200 million from national treasury funds in 2026. The measure removes prior caps on health and indemnity expenses and extends health funding coverage to federal highway and prison police agents.

item.title: Justiça mantém prisão de Márcio Canella após audiência de custódia; ele será levado para Bangu 8
item.description: Justice maintained the pretrial detention of Márcio Canella, former mayor of Belford Roxo and pre-candidate for the Senate under União Brasil, following a custody hearing, for illegal possession of a rifle found in his car during the 6th phase of Operation Unha e Carne. He will be transferred to the Pedrolino Werling de Oliveira Prison (Bangu 8) in Rio de Janeiro. His arrest has destabilized Flávio Bolsonaro’s senatorial slate, with allies deeming his candidacy politically unsustainable.

item.title: Senado aprova MP que destina parte da arrecadação com bets para fundo da Polícia Federal
item.description: The Senate approved a provisional measure redirecting part of the revenue from fixed-odds sports betting (bets) to the Police Federal’s Equipment and Operationalization Fund (Funapol), shifting funds previously allocated to Health and Social Security. The transfer will be phased: 1% in 2026, 2% in 2027, and 3% in 2028, plus an initial R$200 million federal contribution in 2025. Funds may cover health expenses for PF officers and are supplemented by donations and voluntary transfers from states or international entities.

item.title: Cleitinho ameaça decidir só em agosto e PL perde paciência em Minas
item.description: Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos) has once again delayed his decision on running for governor of Minas Gerais, now pushing it to August, causing tension within the state PL. Party leadership is urging a quick decision due to the upcoming state convention on July 23, fearing the delay could harm Flávio Bolsonaro’s electoral slate in the key state. Some PL members advocate nominating Vittorio Medioli as the candidate if Cleitinho does not commit soon.

item.title: Campanha de Lula deve limitar uso de IA em peças e fala em contraponto a Flávio
item.description: Lula's pre-campaign announced it will limit the use of AI in electoral materials, particularly those featuring his image, to contrast with Flávio Bolsonaro's frequent use of AI-generated videos, such as depictions of him piloting aircraft. The strategy aims to portray Lula as authentic and warn against AI-driven disinformation, despite PT allies having previously used AI in videos criticizing Congress and Lula's opponents.

item.title: Ibaneis Rocha desiste de candidatura ao Senado: “Quero descansar”
item.description: Former Distrito Federal governor Ibaneis Rocha (MDB) has withdrawn his Senate candidacy, stating he wants to rest after two terms leading the GDF. He stepped down from office within the incompatibilization period and will return to Brasília only after party conventions on August 5. The decision was confirmed to Metrópoles on the evening of July 8.

item.title: Parlamentar expõe regalias que senadores recebem após eleição: ‘Vocês que pagam’; veja vídeo
item.description: Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos-MG) released a video exposing the privileges senators receive after election, including a luxury functional apartment, optional housing allowance, luxury cars, private security, exclusive elevator, and lifetime health plan. He criticizes these benefits as being funded by the public, contrasting them with the financial and security struggles of most Brazilians, and urges citizens to stop idolizing politicians and hold them accountable.

item.title: Senado aprova projeto contra ligações indesejadas de cobrança e telemarketing
item.description: The Senate approved a bill creating the National Telephone Registry and Number Validation System (CadÚnico Telefônico) to block unwanted telemarketing and debt collection calls. Proposed by Senator Ana Paula Lobato (PSB-MA) and reported favorably by Senator Laércio Oliveira (PP-SE), the bill imposes fines of up to 50,000 reais on non-compliant companies and will now proceed to the Chamber of Deputies for review.

item.title: Zema chama operação da PF contra Bolsonaro de ‘suspeita’ e cobra ação contra mulher de Moraes
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo-MG), a presidential pre-candidate, called the Federal Police operation against Jair Bolsonaro 'extremely suspicious,' arguing that Justice Alexandre de Moraes should have investigated his wife, Viviane Barci de Moraes, over a R$129 million contract with Banco Master. The search of Bolsonaro’s residence, ordered by Moraes after the ex-president declared ownership of eight firearms, found no weapons, despite the Army reporting two registered weapons missing. Zema accused the STF of prioritizing personal interests over national ones.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Lula e Flávio empatam no primeiro e segundo turno em SP, diz pesquisa
item.description: Lula and Flávio Dino are tied in polls for the 2026 elections in São Paulo, both in the first and second round, according to a newly released survey. The result reflects intense competition between the two leading candidates in Brazil’s largest electoral college. The poll did not specify margins of error or detailed methodology.

item.title: Procuradoria vê propaganda eleitoral antecipada e apoia ação contra Lula
item.description: The Regional Electoral Prosecutor's Office in São Paulo concluded that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva conducted premature electoral campaigning by explicitly asking for votes for pre-candidates Simone Tebet and Marina Silva during a federal government event in May 2026. The office recommended upholding the lawsuit filed by Partido Missão and condemning the involved parties, stating the statement had a 'clear electoral character' and violated electoral law prohibiting vote requests before the official campaign period. If the TRE-SP accepts the opinion, Lula, Tebet, and Marina Silva could face fines and sanctions for premature electoral propaganda.

item.title: Senado aprova medida provisória que libera R$ 15 bilhões para financiar exportações em meio à ameaça de tarifa dos EUA
item.description: The Senate approved a provisional measure authorizing up to R$15 billion in new financing lines for Brazilian exporters, drawing from the Export Guarantee Fund and other budgetary sources. The measure, already passed by the Chamber of Deputies, aims to counter the impact of trade barriers, particularly the looming 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, and will be implemented by BNDES. It now awaits presidential sanction.

item.title: Davi cancela sessão do Congresso por falta de acordo sobre vetos
item.description: Senator Davi Alcolumbre, president of the National Congress, canceled the deliberative session scheduled for Thursday (9) due to lack of agreement among party leaders on the voting of presidential vetoes. Despite negotiations between the government and party leaderships, consensus could not be reached, especially in the Chamber of Deputies, where even leaders from the same party disagreed on which vetoes should be analyzed. Alcolumbre stated that holding the session without agreement could prevent obtaining the necessary quorum and that he will continue seeking understanding to define a consensual agenda before calling a new session.

item.title: Novo cobra suspensão de pagamentos após aumento de publicidade de Lula
item.description: The Novo Party filed a lawsuit and submitted a representation to the TCU (Federal Court of Accounts) challenging the spending of the Presidency’s Secretariat of Communication during Sidônio Palmeira’s management, citing excessive advertising linked to President Lula. The party seeks to suspend payments, arguing the expenses are irregular and potentially illegal. Novo claims the spending constitutes improper use of public funds for government self-promotion.

item.title: Senado aprova medida provisória que destina parte de arrecadação com bets à Polícia Federal
item.description: The Senate approved a provisional measure allocating up to 3% of revenue from fixed-odds betting (bets) to the Police Federal Equipment and Operationalization Fund (Funapol), phased in as 1% in 2026, 2% in 2027, and 3% from 2028 onward. Funds will be reallocated from social security without creating new mandatory expenditures, and the fund may also receive voluntary transfers, donations, and finance health expense reimbursements for federal, highway, and prison police. The measure heads to presidential sanction unchanged.

item.title: STF confirma cota racial em fundos eleitorais
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) upheld the rule requiring political parties to allocate 30% of the Party Fund and the Special Campaign Financing Fund to candidacies of Black and brown individuals. The decision also allows parties to compensate, over the next four elections, any shortfalls in meeting this racial quota. The measure aims to increase Black representation in Brazilian politics.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei sobre a sinalização de acessibilidade, mas veta a troca do símbolo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed Law 15.459/26, expanding mandatory accessibility signage in Brazil, but vetoed the proposal to replace the current wheelchair symbol with the new UN model. The veto was justified due to lack of consultation with disability organizations and the risk of creating additional barriers by changing a widely recognized symbol. The law retains mandatory signage on tactile paths, tactile maps, and circulation areas, and requires the symbol to identify only genuinely accessible spaces and services.

item.title: Senado aprova aumentar repasses de impostos sobre bets para a PF
item.description: The Senate approved the substitute of the Provisional Measure to increase tax revenue sharing from betting activities to the Federal Police, allocating 3% of total collections to Funapol in a staggered manner (1% in 2026, 2% in 2027, 3% in 2028). The measure allows for an initial investment of R$ 200 million this year and extends the scope to the Federal Highway Police and Federal Penitentiary Police, while also permitting contributions from federal entities and private donors.

item.title: Mulher arruma enguiço com 20, diz Valdemar sobre extinguir cargo no PL
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, ruled out replacing Michelle Bolsonaro as head of the National PL Women's Wing, stating that appointing another woman could cause dissatisfaction among party members. To avoid conflict, he chose to abolish the national presidency of PL Women and grant autonomy to state structures. Michelle resigned on June 30 to focus on her family, following tensions with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, whom she accused of humiliating and mistreating her, though she later denied any disagreement.

item.title: Tarcísio de Freitas sobre Simone Tebet e Marina Silva: 'Levaram cartão vermelho de MS e AC'
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized pre-candidates for the Senate Marina Silva (Rede) and Simone Tebet (PSB), stating they 'received a red card' in Mato Grosso do Sul and Acre. The remarks were made during a closed meeting with Republicanos pre-candidates and shared in a video on social media. The comments were delivered on Wednesday, January 8.

item.title: Senado aprova crédito de R$ 15 bi para exportadores afetados por tarifaço e guerra no Oriente Médio
item.description: The Senate approved a provisional measure releasing R$15 billion in credit for Brazilian exporters affected by U.S. tariffs and the Middle East war. The financing, part of the Brazil Sovereign Plan, will cover operational expenses such as payroll, equipment purchases, and technology investment, prioritizing high-tech and strategically relevant sectors. The measure now awaits presidential sanction.

item.title: Carioca, Tarcísio critica Marina e Tebet por se candidatarem em SP
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized former ministers Marina Silva and Simone Tebet for running for Senate in São Paulo without being born in the state, despite his own non-native status. He argued that candidates should have a connection to the state they seek to represent.

item.title: Renan Santos rebate Flávio Bolsonaro: 'É especialista em defender inimigos'
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão), a pre-candidate for the Presidency of the Republic, rebutted criticism from Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) for not having visited the United States, stating that the senator is 'an expert in defending enemies'. The statement came amid mutual accusations between the two, sparking repercussions in the national political landscape.

item.title: Novo líder do PT diz que vai atuar para distensionar relação de Lula e Alcolumbre
item.description: The new PT Senate leader, Camilo Santana, said he will work to ease tensions between President Lula and Congress President Davi Alcolumbre to advance government agendas such as ending the 6×1 work scale and the Security PEC. He noted he has spoken with Lula multiple times and expects them to meet soon. Santana took over after Teresa Leitão stepped down to become the government’s Senate leader.

item.title: General posta ironia a Flávio: "Nunca mais um Bolsonaro no Planalto"
item.description: Brazilian Army reserve general Paulo Chagas used social media to mock the potential 2026 presidential candidacy of Flávio Bolsonaro, stating 'we will never again have a Bolsonaro in the Planalto' and calling for the exclusion of the PT from power. He described Bolsonaro's rise as a personal power project born from ideological vacuum, reiterating prior criticisms made in December 2025.

item.title: Os planos de Haddad para avançar no interior de São Paulo em disputa contra Tarcísio
item.description: Fernando Haddad, the PT's pre-candidate for governor of São Paulo, said the state's interior is paying a high price for Donald Trump's tariff, supported by bolsonaristas, and for the lack of public security in goods transport, which has led rural producers to hire private security, posing a risk of militia emergence. He noted that under Lula's government, the Plano Safra reached a record R$ 610 billion, with reduced interest rates and expanded international markets for Brazilian products, driving agribusiness growth.

item.title: Questionado em 2022 por ser carioca, Tarcísio critica Tebet e Marina por se lançarem candidatas por SP
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized Senate pre-candidates Marina Silva and Simone Tebet for running in São Paulo despite their political roots in Acre and Mato Grosso do Sul, accusing them of not having built their careers in the state. Tarcísio, who also changed his electoral domicile from Brasília to São José dos Campos in 2022 (a case later dismissed), argued they would not be elected in their home states nor in São Paulo. The remarks came after a Datafolha poll showed Marina and Tebet leading his allies in the Senate race.

item.title: Tarcísio de Freitas sobre Simone Tebet e Marina Silva: ‘Levaram cartão vermelho de MS e AC’
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized Senate pre-candidates Marina Silva and Simone Tebet, claiming they lack sufficient ties to São Paulo and received a 'red card' from Mato Grosso do Sul and Acre, where they were previously elected. Despite not being born in São Paulo, Tarcísio argues the state should not be used as a 'stepping stone' by politicians from other states. A Datafolha poll shows Marina and Tebet leading the Senate race with 18% and 16%, ahead of Tarcísio-backed candidates.

item.title: STF valida regra que reserva 30% dos fundos eleitorais para candidaturas negras e mantém compensação a partidos
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court upheld the 2024 constitutional amendment that mandates 30% of the Party Fund and Special Campaign Financing Fund (FEFC) be allocated to Black and mixed-race candidacies, affirming it as a legitimate affirmative action policy. The ruling also permits parties to compensate, over the next four elections, for funds not previously allocated to Black candidacies without immediate sanctions, rejecting claims that this constitutes unconstitutional amnesty.

item.title: Sem candidato, PT considera indicação de Patrus Ananias para o governo de MG, mas deputado busca reeleição na Câmara
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) in Minas Gerais is considering Patrus Ananias, former mayor of Belo Horizonte and ex-minister, as a potential gubernatorial candidate, though he signals he will run for re-election to the Chamber of Deputies. While seen as a unifying figure within the party, he states he has not been officially approached and has already launched his re-election campaign. The PT-MG leadership says it continues internal and allied-party dialogue to build a strong gubernatorial slate focused on re-electing Lula and expanding legislative representation.

item.title: Alcolumbre freia ofensiva bolsonarista e não deve pautar urgência do homeschooling
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre signaled he will not prioritize urgency to vote on the homeschooling regulation bill before the parliamentary recess, despite pressure from Bolsonarists. The urgency request, led by Magno Malta and backed by Flávio Bolsonaro’s allies, has only 25 signatures—below the 41 needed—and faces resistance due to lack of Senate support and Alcolumbre’s desire to avoid escalating tensions with the Lula government, which opposes the measure.

item.title: Damares cobra provas de fala de Lula sobre plano de saúde e IR
item.description: Senator Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF) filed two requests demanding the federal government present the studies and documents supporting President Lula's statement that 'the poor pay for the rich's health plan'. The requests were directed to the Ministries of Finance and Health, seeking technical data to substantiate the president's claim.

item.title: Carioca, Tarcísio critica Tebet e Marina por disputarem o Senado em São Paulo
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) criticized former ministers Simone Tebet (PSB) and Marina Silva (Rede) for running for Senate in São Paulo despite not being natives of the state, arguing they served their home states and would not be elected there. He noted he also lacked direct ties to SP when Bolsonaro nominated him in 2022. According to a Datafolha poll, Marina leads with 18%, followed by Tebet at 16% and Ricardo Salles at 13%, all technically tied within the margin of error.

item.title: Republicanos analisará pedido de expulsão de Manga por vídeo na sede do União Brasil
item.description: The São Paulo branch of the Republicans party is reviewing a request to expel Sorocaba Mayor Rodrigo Manga for posting a video at the União Brasil headquarters declaring support for his wife’s federal deputy candidacy. Former São Paulo city councilor Atílio Francisco da Silva claims Manga violated party loyalty rules by openly backing a candidate from another party, warranting suspension or expulsion. Manga insists his support is personal and not incompatible with his affiliation, noting both parties back Governor Tarcísio de Freitas’ re-election and Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential bid.
